finite_operation.text:
Finite operation
Status
Done
Final response

The explicit noisy-recovery protocol is valid under the stated localized one-fault model and has been fully preserved. No further edits are pending.

The protocol measures all six horizontal 
𝑋
𝑋
XX gauges and all six vertical 
𝑍
𝑍
ZZ gauges in each complete round, constructs the full four-bit stabilizer syndrome, and accepts only when two consecutive complete syndrome vectors agree. It terminates within four rounds when the input is clean and at most one localized bad location occurs.

The ordinary proof gives exactly the required guarantees:

Clean input plus one localized fault: the accepted syndrome is either the pre-fault zero syndrome or the actual post-fault syndrome. Recovery therefore leaves either the original correctable error or a gauge operator.
One correctable input error and no new fault: two rounds suffice, and the recovery removes the error modulo gauge.
Coherent faults and weak instruments: the subsystem error-span proof handles coherent Pauli expansions. The actual finite-strength meter enters through the independently verified exact completely positive good/bad decomposition, rather than pretending its measurements are projective or interpreting a channel norm as a probability.

The exhaustive discrete check covers 6,400 scheduled histories, including 100 errors in the larger one-
𝑋
X/one-
𝑍
Z correctable family and every possible four-bit faulty-round report. Of these, 3,200 faults are encountered before adaptive stopping. There are zero violations of either guarantee and zero flagged outcomes under the admitted one-fault model.

The complete report is:

new_research/finite_operation/NOISY_BACON_SHOR_RECOVERY.txt

Its executable check and output are:

new_research/finite_operation/check_bacon_shor_recovery.py
new_research/finite_operation/bacon_shor_recovery_check.json

The report explicitly charges up to 48 gauge meters, 72 physical Hadamards, and 48 local phase corrections, plus initialization, cooldown, routing, controller, and idle-time costs. It retains the failed bitwise-majority construction.

Both numerical pair-union estimates—approximately 0.00193 for the meter-only model and 0.0096648905755 when the stated H and phase-operation errors are added—are labeled strictly as clean-input recovery-episode bounds modulo correctable output. They are not repeated-cycle logical error rates or threshold estimates. Persistent apparatus faults, residual errors crossing episode boundaries, and physical reset remain explicit conditions, with the separate reset certificate referenced.
